bull_bear.body:
- Pharma-grade and food-grade accreditation stack retained during FY2025-26 - ISO 9001:2015, EDQM, ISO 22000 food safety, KOSHER and Halal - which is the qualifying set for supplying regulated pharmaceutical and food customers
- Operating yield and utility efficiency: profit growth was attributed by management to 'better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel', with power and fuel cost down 4.98%
- Ability to switch to imported raw material when global gelatine/raw-material prices fall, easing pressure on domestic raw-material supplies
- Significant influence over India Gelatine and Chemicals Limited (IGCL), treated as an associate because the Company together with its promoters holds more than 20% of IGCL's equity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Substitution by plant-based gelatin alternatives, plus cultural and religious prohibitions on animal-source gelatine — Management names this as the primary market barrier: 'The rise of plant-based gelatin substitutes, fueled by rising demand for vegetarian and vegan goods, is one of the primary market barriers. Traditional gelatin made from animal sources is affected due to this trend'. It attacks the core product rather than a segment, so it is structural for a single-product gelatine maker.
- Raw material availability and price, including reliance on imports versus domestic supply — The cautionary statement lists 'raw material availability, import and exports of raw material and finished goods' among the factors outside the Company's control. The FY26 benefit came from a global gelatine price fall in the second half that cut raw-material cost and let the Company import at competitive prices, easing 'pressure in domestic raw material supplies' - the same mechanism reverses if global prices rise.
- Single-segment, single-product-family concentration — 'The Company is engaged in only one segment, namely, manufacture and sale of gelatine and related products like assein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP) and as such there are no reportable segments as per Ind AS-108.' With gelatine 70.77% and DCP 29.15% of turnover, there is no diversification to absorb a shock to gelatine demand or pricing.
- Gelatine realisation deflation - price risk decoupling volume growth from revenue — During FY2025-26 gelatine sales volume rose 16.17% but the average selling price of gelatine fell 5.20%; DCP volume rose 11.35% with its average selling price up 17.17%. The gelatine price direction is set by the global market, not by the Company, so volume gains can be offset by realisation.
- Energy and fuel cost exposure, principally coal — Power and fuel cost fell 4.98% 'due to decrease in the coal prices and consumption', and profit growth was attributed to 'better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel'. A material part of the FY26 margin expansion is therefore a commodity input tailwind that can reverse.
- Geopolitical instability affecting global trade flows — 'Prolonged geopolitical instability, including the middle-east conflict, may continue to impact global trade flows and overall market sentiments.' This bears on both imported raw material and exports, which grew sharply in FY26.
- Government regulation and taxation changes — The cautionary statement lists 'government regulations, changes in taxation' among factors that could make a significant difference to operations and over which the Company has no direct control. The business is also subject to food-safety, pollution-control, legal-metrology and factories legislation per the secretarial audit scope.
- Demand and macro conditions plus natural calamities outside management control — The forward-looking-statement caveat names 'economic conditions, affecting demand and supply ... natural calamities, on which the Company does not have any direct control' as reasons actual results may differ from stated expectations.

outlook.body:
- Opportunistically import/purchase raw material while global gelatine and raw-material prices are depressed, to secure competitive input costs and relieve pressure on domestic raw-material supplies
- Stay a single-segment gelatine player - gelatine plus related products ossein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP) - with no reportable segments under Ind AS-108
- Maintain the pharma- and food-grade accreditation stack (ISO 9001:2015, EDQM, ISO 22000 via DNV, KOSHER, Halal) as a stated commitment to the highest levels of product and customer-service quality
- Build strategic presence in the wider Indian gelatine industry through the 14.14% direct stake in India Gelatine and Chemicals Limited, which with promoter holdings takes the group above 20% and gives significant influence
- Make CSR a key business process for sustainable development, integrating CSR values with business objectives across environment, education, healthcare and rural development around its operations
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's FY2025-26 disclosures describe efficiency and utility capex at its Jabalpur works rather than any gelatine capacity expansion. Under conservation of energy it installed an Ultra-filtration (UF) Plant for gelatine concentration, thereby eliminating use of the old SSP Evaporator to save on steam and electricity, and replaced steam radiators with hot water radiators to reduce steam consumption. For environment conservation it installed rain water harvesting and revamped the CICON Plant to utilise treated water for process, reducing fresh water consumption. On alternate energy, 'The solar plant within the Factory premises commissioned', with capital investment on energy conservation equipment (Solar Plant) stated at Rs 8.89 Crores. On technology absorption, 'Process control for improvement of product quality and the implementation of SAP is currently underway and progressing as planned', with the benefit described as improvement in product mix giving better realization; no technology was imported. R&D was expensed only - recurring R&D expenditure with nil capital R&D. No installed-capacity table, no new plant, line or greenfield project and no commissioning timetable for capacity is disclosed in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global gelatine market valued at USD 3.40 billion in 2025 and projected to grow from USD 3.60 billion in 2026 to USD 6.58 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 7.83%
- Indian gelatine market expected to register a CAGR of around 7.5% over the next few years
- Rising consumer awareness of gelatin's collagen-driven health benefits - joint health, skin elasticity, hair strength - driving demand in nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals
- Widening application base across food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, photography and dietary supplements
- Indian pharmaceutical demand pull: drugs and pharmaceuticals exports up ~2% YoY in FY2025-26, India the 3rd largest pharma industry by volume with 60,000+ generic drugs across 60+ therapeutic categories, and continued Government PLI schemes promoting domestic manufacture of key pharmaceutical ingredients and generic medicines
- Threat from plant-based gelatin substitutes driven by vegetarian/vegan demand and sustainability/ethics preferences, plus cultural and religious prohibitions impeding market growth
- Global gelatine price reduction cut raw-material prices significantly in the second half of the year, an input-cost tailwind the Company is using to import at competitive prices
- Margin levers cited for the year: better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel, with power and fuel cost down 4.98% on lower coal prices and consumption
- Mix and pricing: gelatine 70.77% of turnover and DCP 29.15%; gelatine average selling price down 5.20% while DCP average selling price rose 17.17%, against volume growth of 16.17% in gelatine and 11.35% in DCP
- Prolonged geopolitical instability including the middle-east conflict may continue to impact global trade flows and overall market sentiment

- EDQM Certification from the European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines and Healthcare
- DNV Management System Certification for Food Safety Management System Standard (ISO 22000:2005)
- KOSHER Certification
- Halal Assurance System Certification

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global gelatine market valued at USD 3.40 billion in 2025 and projected to grow from USD 3.60 billion in 2026 to USD 6.58 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 7.83%
- Indian gelatine market expected to register a CAGR of around 7.5% over the next few years
- Rising consumer awareness of gelatin's collagen-driven health benefits - joint health, skin elasticity, hair strength - driving demand in nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals
- Widening application base across food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, photography and dietary supplements
- Indian pharmaceutical demand pull: drugs and pharmaceuticals exports up ~2% YoY in FY2025-26, India the 3rd largest pharma industry by volume with 60,000+ generic drugs across 60+ therapeutic categories, and continued Government PLI schemes promoting domestic manufacture of key pharmaceutical ingredients and generic medicines
- Threat from plant-based gelatin substitutes driven by vegetarian/vegan demand and sustainability/ethics preferences, plus cultural and religious prohibitions impeding market growth
- Global gelatine price reduction cut raw-material prices significantly in the second half of the year, an input-cost tailwind the Company is using to import at competitive prices
- Margin levers cited for the year: better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel, with power and fuel cost down 4.98% on lower coal prices and consumption
- Mix and pricing: gelatine 70.77% of turnover and DCP 29.15%; gelatine average selling price down 5.20% while DCP average selling price rose 17.17%, against volume growth of 16.17% in gelatine and 11.35% in DCP
- Prolonged geopolitical instability including the middle-east conflict may continue to impact global trade flows and overall market sentiment

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Opportunistically import/purchase raw material while global gelatine and raw-material prices are depressed, to secure competitive input costs and relieve pressure on domestic raw-material supplies
- Stay a single-segment gelatine player - gelatine plus related products ossein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP) - with no reportable segments under Ind AS-108
- Maintain the pharma- and food-grade accreditation stack (ISO 9001:2015, EDQM, ISO 22000 via DNV, KOSHER, Halal) as a stated commitment to the highest levels of product and customer-service quality
- Build strategic presence in the wider Indian gelatine industry through the 14.14% direct stake in India Gelatine and Chemicals Limited, which with promoter holdings takes the group above 20% and gives significant influence
- Make CSR a key business process for sustainable development, integrating CSR values with business objectives across environment, education, healthcare and rural development around its operations

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's FY2025-26 disclosures describe efficiency and utility capex at its Jabalpur works rather than any gelatine capacity expansion. Under conservation of energy it installed an Ultra-filtration (UF) Plant for gelatine concentration, thereby eliminating use of the old SSP Evaporator to save on steam and electricity, and replaced steam radiators with hot water radiators to reduce steam consumption. For environment conservation it installed rain water harvesting and revamped the CICON Plant to utilise treated water for process, reducing fresh water consumption. On alternate energy, 'The solar plant within the Factory premises commissioned', with capital investment on energy conservation equipment (Solar Plant) stated at Rs 8.89 Crores. On technology absorption, 'Process control for improvement of product quality and the implementation of SAP is currently underway and progressing as planned', with the benefit described as improvement in product mix giving better realization; no technology was imported. R&D was expensed only - recurring R&D expenditure with nil capital R&D. No installed-capacity table, no new plant, line or greenfield project and no commissioning timetable for capacity is disclosed in this bundle.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Pharma-grade and food-grade accreditation stack retained during FY2025-26 - ISO 9001:2015, EDQM, ISO 22000 food safety, KOSHER and Halal - which is the qualifying set for supplying regulated pharmaceutical and food customers
- Operating yield and utility efficiency: profit growth was attributed by management to 'better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel', with power and fuel cost down 4.98%
- Ability to switch to imported raw material when global gelatine/raw-material prices fall, easing pressure on domestic raw-material supplies
- Significant influence over India Gelatine and Chemicals Limited (IGCL), treated as an associate because the Company together with its promoters holds more than 20% of IGCL's equity

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Substitution by plant-based gelatin alternatives, plus cultural and religious prohibitions on animal-source gelatine — Management names this as the primary market barrier: 'The rise of plant-based gelatin substitutes, fueled by rising demand for vegetarian and vegan goods, is one of the primary market barriers. Traditional gelatin made from animal sources is affected due to this trend'. It attacks the core product rather than a segment, so it is structural for a single-product gelatine maker.
- Raw material availability and price, including reliance on imports versus domestic supply — The cautionary statement lists 'raw material availability, import and exports of raw material and finished goods' among the factors outside the Company's control. The FY26 benefit came from a global gelatine price fall in the second half that cut raw-material cost and let the Company import at competitive prices, easing 'pressure in domestic raw material supplies' - the same mechanism reverses if global prices rise.
- Single-segment, single-product-family concentration — 'The Company is engaged in only one segment, namely, manufacture and sale of gelatine and related products like assein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP) and as such there are no reportable segments as per Ind AS-108.' With gelatine 70.77% and DCP 29.15% of turnover, there is no diversification to absorb a shock to gelatine demand or pricing.
- Gelatine realisation deflation - price risk decoupling volume growth from revenue — During FY2025-26 gelatine sales volume rose 16.17% but the average selling price of gelatine fell 5.20%; DCP volume rose 11.35% with its average selling price up 17.17%. The gelatine price direction is set by the global market, not by the Company, so volume gains can be offset by realisation.
- Energy and fuel cost exposure, principally coal — Power and fuel cost fell 4.98% 'due to decrease in the coal prices and consumption', and profit growth was attributed to 'better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel'. A material part of the FY26 margin expansion is therefore a commodity input tailwind that can reverse.
- Geopolitical instability affecting global trade flows — 'Prolonged geopolitical instability, including the middle-east conflict, may continue to impact global trade flows and overall market sentiments.' This bears on both imported raw material and exports, which grew sharply in FY26.
- Government regulation and taxation changes — The cautionary statement lists 'government regulations, changes in taxation' among factors that could make a significant difference to operations and over which the Company has no direct control. The business is also subject to food-safety, pollution-control, legal-metrology and factories legislation per the secretarial audit scope.
- Demand and macro conditions plus natural calamities outside management control — The forward-looking-statement caveat names 'economic conditions, affecting demand and supply ... natural calamities, on which the Company does not have any direct control' as reasons actual results may differ from stated expectations.
